validity.recommendation: No change needed; row is a real, correctly-classified operating dedicated pipeline. Diameter remains a legitimate blank (see caveat).
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently. DNP Limited (DNPL) is a live, active Government-of-Assam JV company (CIN U51410AS2007SGC008410, GSTIN 18AACCD8810C1ZY) that files audited annual reports through FY2024-25 (https://www.dnpl.co.in/assets/uploads/financial/annual-report-17669887791597877144.pdf), and the pipeline is separately itemised as an authorised, operational asset in PNGRB's regulator-published 'Operational Dedicated Natural Gas Pipelines' table (current June-2025 edition, https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20250630_NGPL.pdf, printed page listing row '19.01.NGPL Duliajan to Numaligarh, Entity: DNPL, Auth. Date 26.03.2009, Authorised Length 194.00 km, Authorised Capacity 1.20 MMSCMD, Operating Length 192.00 km, Assam'). url_verifier gives a false-negative HTTP 200 on this PDF (documented large-PDF limitation for this country); confirmed locally with `pdftotext -layout` at line 169. Two genuinely independent origins (the JV company itself, and India's oil/gas regulator) agree the pipeline exists and is operating -> tier=high. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is reasonable -- this is a ~190 km bulk gas-transport trunk line from OIL's Duliajan gas source area to NRL's refinery at Numaligarh, not a gathering/feeder or distribution line; neither source uses the literal word 'transmission' but both describe exactly that function. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 35-pipeline India-gas roster supplied for this sweep -- no other row names Duliajan or Numaligarh; this is not a relabel/segment double-count of any other GEM pipeline. SPEC/LENGTH CAVEAT: GEM's LengthKnown=194.00 km matches PNGRB's 'Authorised Length' column exactly; DNPL's own site (https://www.dnpl.co.in/profile) separately states 'Pipeline Length: 192 km', which matches PNGRB's 'Operating Length' column exactly. These are not a conflict -- they are two different, both-correct readings (as-authorised vs as-built/operating), off by only 1%. Recommend keeping GEM's 194.00 (the authorised figure) as-is; a ResearcherNotes line noting the 192 km operating figure would be a nice-to-have but is not a correctness issue. DIAMETER (still blank): a third-party market database summary (offshore-technology.com, sourced from GlobalData, https://www.offshore-technology.com/marketdata/duliajan-numaligarh-gas-pipeline-india/) claims 'maximum diameter of 16 inches', but the SAME page also states the pipeline is 250 km long and lists 'Engineers India' among the owners -- both demonstrably wrong per the two independent primary sources above (194/192 km; AGCL/NRL/OIL ownership, see the paired attribution finding). Given that internal error, I am not staging the 16-inch figure as a diameter fill off this single, evidently unreliable source -- flagging it as an unconfirmed lead only, per the instruction to leave weak fields blank rather than force a number.

validity.recommendation: Correct Owner on the operators/owners tab (oo_sheet_row 2495) from 'DNP Ltd 100%' to the actual JV equity holders: Owner1 = Assam Gas Company Limited (AGCL) 51%, Owner2 = Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL) 26%, Owner3 = Oil India Limited (OIL) 23%. Leave Operator = 'DNP Ltd' unchanged -- that is correct, DNPL is genuinely the operating entity.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet lists Owner1 = 'DNP Ltd' 100%, which is the same value as Operator -- but DNP Limited does not own itself; it is a joint-venture SPV whose shares are held by three parent companies. DNPL's own audited FY2024-25 annual report gives an explicit 'Shareholding Pattern as on 31-03-2025' table: Assam Gas Company Limited 51%, Numaligarh Refinery Limited 26%, Oil India Limited 23% (page with the shareholding table, https://www.dnpl.co.in/assets/uploads/financial/annual-report-17669887791597877144.pdf -- verified locally via pdftotext, the exact figures also appear on the company's public profile page https://www.dnpl.co.in/profile, both giving identical 51/26/23 splits). I am treating this as tier=medium rather than high: both documents originate from DNPL itself (one is its public marketing/profile page, the other its statutory audited annual report), so while they are two distinct document types with two different dates, they are not two independently-operated organisations corroborating each other the way PNGRB + DNPL do elsewhere in this row -- I could not find a fully third-party (non-DNPL) source stating the ownership percentages, and note that a market-database page (offshore-technology.com/GlobalData) names a different, apparently wrong fourth party ('Engineers India') as an owner, which I am discounting given that same page's other factual errors (see paired existence finding). Recommend the correction above; not auto-applying per standing rules.

fills.researcher_notes: PNGRB lists the pipeline under 'Operational Dedicated Natural Gas Pipelines' (current, June 2025 edition -- verified locally, url_verifier false-negatives on this large PDF); DNPL's own site describes the pipeline as an active, ongoing operation (annual report also confirms ongoing commercial operation since 2011, still filing FY2024-25 results). Two independent origins.
Both PNGRB's natural gas pipeline register and DNPL's own description ('transportation of natural gas from Duliajan to Numaligarh Refinery Limited') confirm the commodity is natural gas.

Neither source uses the literal word 'transmission', but both describe a ~190-200 km bulk gas-transport trunk line moving gas in bulk from a source area (Duliajan) to a single large industrial offtaker (Numaligarh refinery) -- functionally a transmission trunk line, not gathering/feeder or distribution. Tier held to medium because the classification is inferential rather than a verbatim label.

DNPL's profile page states construction 'completed February 28, 2011'; its FY2024-25 annual report (CSR annexure) independently states 'The Company started its commercial operation from 1st April, 2011'. StartYear1=2011 is corroborated by both. Held to tier=medium/independent=false because both documents are DNPL's own first-party publications (no fully external/third-party source found for the exact year; PNGRB's listed 'Auth. Date' of 26.03.2009 is an authorisation date, not a commissioning date, per this sweep's standing guidance, so it neither confirms nor contradicts 2011). Note: profile page implies Feb 2011 completion vs annual report's April 2011 commercial-operation start -- consistent with a short commissioning/trial-run gap; StartMonth1 is left unproposed given the ambiguity between the two dates.

PNGRB's current (June 2025) dedicated-pipeline register gives Authorised Capacity = 1.20 MMSCMD for this exact line -- matches the sheet exactly. url_verifier false-negatives on this large PDF (documented country-level limitation); confirmed locally via pdftotext at line 169: 'Duliajan to Numaligarh DNPL 26.03.2009 194.00 1.20 192.00 Assam'. Single-source (regulator only; DNPL's own materials do not state a capacity figure) so held to tier=medium despite the source being authoritative.

PNGRB's register gives 'Authorised Length' = 194.00 km, matching the sheet exactly (verified locally, url_verifier false-negatives on this large PDF). DNPL's own profile page separately gives 'Pipeline Length: 192 km', which matches PNGRB's own separate 'Operating Length' column of 192.00 km -- i.e. two independent origins (regulator + company) agree on both readings once you separate as-authorised from as-built. Recommend keeping 194.00 (authorised) as the sheet value; the 192 km operating figure is a documented, sourced nuance worth a ResearcherNotes mention but not a correction.

Both DNPL's own materials and PNGRB's register confirm Duliajan-to-Numaligarh routing entirely within Assam, India. DNPL's profile page additionally states the route passes through five Assam districts (not itemised there), consistent with an intra-Assam trunk line; district-level fields left unproposed as no source itemises them.

DNPL's homepage states 'DNP Limited operates a natural gas transportation pipeline from Duliajan to Numaligarh'; PNGRB's register lists 'Entity: DNPL' for this exact line. Two independent origins confirm DNP Ltd (DNP Limited) as operator -- this value is correct and distinct from the Owner question below.

NOT adding a ref to confirm the current value -- both sources found contradict 'DNP Ltd 100%' as Owner. DNPL's own profile page and its FY2024-25 audited annual report (Shareholding Pattern as on 31-03-2025) both give: Assam Gas Company Limited (AGCL) 51%, Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL) 26%, Oil India Limited (OIL) 23%. DNP Ltd is the operating SPV, not its own owner. See the paired attribution concern in the validity array for the recommended correction; left UNRESOLVED here rather than staging a ref against a value I believe is wrong, per the no-auto-apply / no-orphan-ref rules.

summary: P3310 (Duliajan-Numaligarh Gas Pipeline) is a real, correctly-classified operating pipeline -- existence and status confirmed independently via PNGRB's current dedicated-pipeline register and DNPL's own audited filings, which also confirm Length (194.00 km authorised / 192 km operating, both cited), Capacity (1.20 MMSCMD), StartYear1=2011, Fuel, Location, and Operator; no duplicate against the 35-pipeline roster. One genuine attribution concern: Owner is recorded as 'DNP Ltd 100%' but DNPL's own audited annual report gives the actual JV shareholders as AGCL 51% / NRL 26% / OIL 23% -- recommend correcting on the operators/owners tab. Diameter stays UNRESOLVED/blank: the only lead (a GlobalData/offshore-technology.com summary claiming 16 inch) also contains a demonstrably wrong length and owner, so it was not staged.
